evidence_summary: Twelve healthy adults chewed thawed California Wonder, CH-19 Sweet or cayenne. California Wonder was a nonpungent cultivar without detected capsinoids or capsaicinoids in the authors’ characterization. Autonomic and thermal outcomes provide no handwriting or patient estimate.
First posted 2009-10-21 (estimated field). Metabolic outcome only. ClinicalTrials.gov returned no posted results or adverse-event summary.

The 78-participant parallel placebo trial collected repeated symptom checklists over 28 days. Published differences were dry mouth and leg cramps, each p=.04. It supplied no individual sleepy or alert estimate.

2012-03-27 application names bell pepper within a broader genus and describes capsaicinoid-containing pepper powder plus wolfberry. Its drowsiness and fatigue assertions lacked a verified clinical outcome comparison.

A rotenone-exposed rat study reported more cylinder rears at the middle and high extract doses and under levodopa co-treatment. The fruit cultivar was unspecified and the extract contained capsaicin and dihydrocapsaicin. No grilled pepper or gait speed.

Twelve physically active men taking 12 mg oral capsiate recorded 66.4 ± 4.2 vs 67.1 ± 4.8 seconds for 400 m (p=.046) and 893.9 ± 46.8 vs 915.2 ± 67.6 seconds for 3000 m (p=.015). Running is distinct from walking slowness.

Twenty-one amateur male athletes took a total of 24 mg oral capsiate across two doses. Ten-kilometer running was 45.07 ± 6.41 vs 45.13 ± 6.73 minutes (p=.828). A later review mislabeled this protocol as cycling and gave a single 12 mg dose.

status: strong related whole food and composite
evidence_summary: Older Tianjin adults (n=2,451). Sweet pepper adjusted sarcopenia ORs .73 (.56–.96) at ≤1 time/week and .66 (.45–.95) at ≥2–3 times/week vs almost never, trend p<.01. Usual-pace 4 m gait and handgrip were diagnosis components. Pepper-specific component effects and preparation were not reported.

Other vegetables in the MIND questionnaire had β −190 (95% CI −262 to −119), p<.001, with total PRO-PD. Mediterranean vegetables including one raw or salad serving had β −95 (−156 to −35.5), p=.02. Survey did not specify bell pepper and no corresponding individual symptom coefficients were published.

status: related perceived exertion and carrier comparator
evidence_summary: Randomized crossover 12 mg purified dihydrocapsiate in canola oil versus microcrystalline cellulose placebo. No reported perceived-fatigue difference during 60-min cycling. Canola carrier was in active capsules only, so the contrast does not isolate the oil or whole pepper.

Publisher abstract accepted 2026-11-02 reports no readiness-to-invest-effort difference under 12 mg capsiate versus placebo in 11 physically active men. No arm estimates or apathy scale. Final article was unavailable at review.

In 181 older Chilean participants, recalled red bell pepper contributed to aggregate dietary polyphenol estimates. Outcomes included handgrip with no pepper-specific comparison or fine-dexterity measure. Gait was not measured.

In a 20-man crossover, 6 mg capsiate increased bench weight vs placebo (2,454.6 ± 448.6 vs 2,354.7 ± 458.6 kg, p=.039). The 12 mg dose gave no improvement. Fine dexterity, grilled foods and Parkinson disease were unrepresented.

In a triple-blind crossover with 25 trained adults, 12 mg dihydrocapsiate versus placebo did not affect bench and squat measures (all p≥.703). Bench press throw velocity 2.82 ± .77 versus 2.82 ± .74 m/s. No individual hand motor or Parkinson endpoint.

EFSA describes 70 healthy Japanese men in a 4-week dihydrocapsiate versus placebo beverage trial. General symptom questionnaires were collected at the first and last day. No item-level sleepiness results in the public opinion or standalone Kajimoto source verified.

In a 2,537-participant 2019 abstract sweet pepper pointed in a similar direction without significance. The 2021 journal n=2,451 report and adjusted sweet pepper result are best treated as potentially overlapping. The conference abstract gives no sweet pepper component estimate.

status: clinical mobility and questionnaire exposure boundary
evidence_summary: Cross-sectional Parkinson sample n=70 with mobility and a 118-item questionnaire. The original Thai-English supplemental questionnaire names chili powder plus green leafy and root vegetables. No named bell pepper or pepper-specific mobility coefficient.
